section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: CCres converts two RISC OS binary resource formats into a stable textual form and can reconstruct the binary files from that text. The supported binary formats are Toolbox Resource files with filetype ,fae and Wimp Template files with filetype ,fec.

The textual form is intended for editing, comparison, searching, translation, and bulk maintenance. It names object classes, field names, symbolic flags, and string contents explicitly, so changes that are awkward in binary editors can be made with ordinary text tools. The text syntax is close to C structure initialiser style, but remains line-oriented and simple enough to be generated and parsed without a full compiler front end.
This manual describes the standalone command-line program ccres, which performs the same conversions without requiring a desktop application.

subsection.title: Command-line behaviour
subsection.p: The command-line program takes exactly two positional arguments: an input filename and an output filename. There are no option switches in the current implementation. The input file type is detected from its contents, not from its name.

definition.name: Toolbox Resource binary
definition.extra: First word is RESF and version is 101

definition-table.definition: Converted to text. The generated text begins with RESF:1.01.

definition.name: Wimp Template binary
definition.extra: Second, third, and fourth header words are zero

definition-table.definition: Converted to text. The generated text begins with Template:.

definition.name: Text file
definition.extra: First sixteen bytes contain no control characters other than LF

definition-table.definition: The first line selects the output binary format. RESF:1.01 selects Toolbox Resource output; Template: selects Wimp Template output.

subsection.p: When the input is text, only two text headers are recognised: RESF:1.01 and Template:. Although older descriptive material mentions RESF version 1.00, the current implementation accepts and writes only RESF version 1.01.

The program recognises text by scanning the first sixteen bytes for control characters. The binary resource and template probes are performed before that text test, so binary files are not mistaken for text merely because their filenames end in .txt.

subsection.title: Overall text grammar
subsection.p: CCres text is line-oriented. During import, linefeeds are replaced internally with string terminators, so each source line is parsed independently. Object bodies are enclosed in braces and nested objects are represented by nested brace blocks.

p.extended-example:
resource-file ::= "RESF:1.01" LF { resource-object }
template-file ::= "Template:" LF { wimp-window } { template-font-data }
resource-object ::= object-name "{" LF { entry-line | nested-object } "}" LF
wimp-window ::= "wimp_window" "{" LF { entry-line | "wimp_icon" block } "}" LF
template-font-data ::= "template_font_data" "{" LF { entry-line } "}" LF
entry-line ::= entry-name ":" value LF
comment ::= "#" text-to-end-of-line

subsection.p: Object names are matched case-insensitively. Entry names should be written exactly as CCres emits them. The parser for entries is effectively case-sensitive at the first character and is designed around the canonical lower-case spellings shown in this chapter.

Within an object body, a colon introduces the value for that entry and causes the remainder of the line to be treated as data. A number sign introduces a comment and causes the remainder of the line to be ignored. Because values and comments consume the rest of the line, braces inside them do not affect object nesting.

subsection.title: Numbers, expressions, and symbolic values
subsection.p: Numeric fields accept more than plain decimal. The shared number parser understands:

Fields of type cmp, bbox, and coord are evaluated as arithmetic expressions rather than simple integers. The operators (), +, -, *, and / are supported. Division is integer division. Expression depth is deliberately small and malformed expressions are reported with a line number.

Many fields use symbolic values instead of raw numbers. Flag fields accept one or more symbolic names separated by vertical bars. Enumeration fields accept a single symbolic name. Residual flag bits that do not correspond to a known symbol are written as 0x... on export and may be read back in that form.
Component-reference fields accept either a numeric component id or the special names toolbox_NULL_COMPONENT and toolbox_WINDOW_FOCUS.

subsection.title: Strings, quoting, and size fields
subsection.p: CCres always exports strings in double quotes. Import does not require quotes, but quoted strings are the canonical form and should be preferred.

Quoted strings may have spaces after the closing quote. Unquoted strings run to the end of the line. Quotes are mainly significant for preserving trailing spaces unambiguously. Unmatched quotes are reported as an input error.
The textual format uses several kinds of string field:

definition-table.definition: Stored in the object's message string table. The associated ..._limit: field may be a number or *.
Stored in the object's ordinary string table. Associated limits behave the same way as message-table strings.
Stored inside a Template window's trailing string area and terminated with carriage return in the binary file.
Stored directly in the structure body. Template names are limited by the binary field width.

subsection.p: For Resource strings, a limit field of * means "allocate only enough space for the current string plus its terminator". If the string is empty and the limit is *, CCres may omit the stored string reference entirely.

For Template strings, the exported size is the allocated byte count in the Template string area. A limit of * means "use the current string length including its carriage-return terminator". If a supplied size is smaller than the string actually needs, CCres increases it and emits a warning rather than silently truncating the data.

subsection.title: Toolbox Resource text format
subsection.p: A Resource text file begins with RESF:1.01 followed by zero or more top-level Toolbox objects. Each object has a class-specific object name and contains a common object header followed by class-specific entries.

definition-table.definition: Supports keyboard shortcuts and all gadget blocks documented later in this chapter.
Version-dependent fields exist for version 1.01 objects.

subsubsection.title: Common object header fields
subsubsection.p: Every top-level Resource object begins with the same three fields.

definition-table.definition: Zero or more of toolbox_OBJECT_CREATE_ON_LOAD, toolbox_OBJECT_SHOW_ON_CREATE, toolbox_OBJECT_SHARED, and toolbox_OBJECT_ANCESTOR.
Object format version stored in the Resource object header.
Object name used for Toolbox references.

subsubsection.title: Window objects
subsubsection.p: window_object is the richest Resource form. It carries the Toolbox-level window metadata, the embedded Wimp window definition, zero or more keyboardshortcut_object blocks, and zero or more gadget blocks.

definition-table.definition: Toolbox window flags such as window_AUTO_OPEN, window_AUTO_CLOSE, and window_IS_TOOL_BAR.

Action code sent when the object is hidden. A blank value means unset.
Stacking order such as wimp_TOP, wimp_BOTTOM, or wimp_HIDDEN.
Wimp window flags, including furniture and scrolling bits.
Extended Wimp window flags such as title-validation use and 3D preferences.
Sprite area reference, exported as hexadecimal.

subsubsection.p: The nested keyboardshortcut_object blocks use these entries:

definition-table.definition: Shortcut show flags such as keyboardshortcut_SHOW_AS_MENU, keyboardshortcut_SHOW_AT_CENTRE, and keyboardshortcut_SHOW_AT_POINTER.
Action or Toolbox event value associated with the key.

subsubsection.title: Window gadget blocks
subsubsection.p: Every gadget block begins with the same three header entries and then adds class-specific entries.

definition-table.definition: Bounding box in window work-area coordinates.

subsubsection.title: Menu objects
subsubsection.p: A menu_object contains the menu header followed by one or more nested Entry blocks.

definition-table.definition: Menu-level flags such as menu_GENERATE_ABOUT_TO_BE_SHOWN, menu_GENERATE_DIALOGUE_COMPLETED, and menu_GENERATE_HAS_BEEN_HIDDEN.

Normal entries use the message table. If menu_ENTRY_IS_SPRITE is set, the same field is stored as an ordinary string naming the sprite.

subsubsection.p: For proginfo_object, a Resource object whose version: field is 101 also accepts visit_url: and visit_url_event:. Later versions do not carry those fields in the current implementation.

subsection.title: Wimp Template text format
subsection.p: A Template text file begins with the literal line Template:. The normal canonical order is:

item.p: One or more top-level wimp_window blocks.
Zero or more top-level template_font_data blocks.

subsection.p: CCres counts top-level brace blocks before conversion, then performs a first pass that consumes only leading wimp_window blocks. For that reason, Template text should keep all window blocks before any template_font_data blocks and should not place other top-level object names in the file.

subsubsection.title: Template window fields
subsubsection.p: Each wimp_window block begins with template_name: and then carries the embedded Wimp window definition.

definition-table.definition: Template name. The binary field is twelve bytes including the terminator, so names longer than eleven visible characters are truncated with a warning.
Title icon flags. These determine which title text entries are legal.
Wimp button-type flags for the work area.

subsubsection.p: The title text or sprite payload is encoded through the same icon-data rules that ordinary wimp_icon blocks use. Depending on the title_flags: bits, the title section may therefore use one of the following entry sets:

subsubsection.title: Template icon blocks
subsubsection.p: Each nested wimp_icon block inside a window uses the common entries below before any icon-data payload entries.

definition-table.definition: Wimp icon flags plus the encoded Wimp button type. Symbolic button types such as wimp_BUTTON_CLICK are accepted in the same field.
Background colour for normal icons and anti-aliased icons.
Anti-aliased icon font handle. This is used instead of icon_fg: when wimp_ICON_ANTI_ALIASED is set.

subsubsection.p: The icon payload entries follow the same six-way selection described for window titles:

subsubsection.title: Template font blocks
subsubsection.p: Optional template_font_data blocks represent entries from the Template font table. Each block accepts exactly these entries:

definition-table.definition: Font name stored in the forty-byte binary field.

subsection.title: Round-tripping and canonical output
subsection.p: CCres does not attempt byte-for-byte recreation of files created by other tools. It recreates equivalent Resource or Template content in its own normal serialisation.
Important consequences of that normalisation are:

item.p: Resource relocation entries are written in ascending offset order.
Superfluous fields that some GUI editors save are omitted when CCres does not use them.
Template text is truncated at the first control character terminator; stray bytes after a terminator are ignored when exporting to text.
Strings are re-emitted in quoted canonical form, and size fields may be normalised to * when they match the minimal required allocation.

subsection.p: For these reasons, binary comparison against an original editor-produced file is not a reliable validation method. The canonical validation loop is text-to-binary-to-text round-tripping and comparison of the textual forms.

section.title: Command-line usage
section.p: The standalone program is invoked as:

infile must be a Toolbox Resource binary, a Wimp Template binary, or a CCres text file beginning with RESF:1.01 or Template:. outfile receives the converted form. When the input is binary, the output is text. When the input is text, the output is either a Resource binary or a Template binary according to the first line of the file.

The program performs a single conversion in the direction implied by the input file. Binary Resource files and binary Template files are converted to text. Text files are converted back into binary using their first line as the format selector.

The current implementation requires exactly two positional arguments and provides no option switches. If the argument count is wrong, the tool exits with an error after printing a short usage summary.

subsection.title: Converting a Toolbox Resource file to text
subsection.p: This is the normal editing path for a Toolbox Resource file.

subsection.title: A minimal Resource text file
subsection.p: This example shows the required outer structure of a Resource text file.

p.extended-example:
RESF:1.01
window_object {
header_flags:
version:102
object_name:"Main"
window_flags:
help_message:""
help_limit:*
sprite_name:""
pointer_limit:0
hotspot:0,0
menu_name:""
default_focus:toolbox_NULL_COMPONENT
show_action:
hide_action:
toolbar_ibl:""
toolbar_itl:""
toolbar_ebl:""
toolbar_etl:""
window.visible:0,0,640,480
window.xscroll:0
window.yscroll:0
window.next:wimp_TOP
window.flags:wimp_WINDOW_MOVEABLE | wimp_WINDOW_NEW_FORMAT
window.title_fg:wimp_COLOUR_BLACK
window.title_bg:wimp_COLOUR_LIGHT_GREY
window.work_fg:wimp_COLOUR_BLACK
window.work_bg:wimp_COLOUR_VERY_LIGHT_GREY
window.scroll_outer:wimp_COLOUR_CREAM
window.scroll_inner:wimp_COLOUR_ORANGE
window.highlight_bg:wimp_COLOUR_LIGHT_GREY
window.extra_flags:
window.extent:0,-480,640,0
window.title_flags:wimp_ICON_TEXT | wimp_ICON_INDIRECTED
window.work_flags:
window.sprite_area:&ffffffff
window.xmin:0
window.ymin:0
window.title_text:"Main window"
window.title_text_limit:*
window.title_valid:""
}

subsection.title: A minimal Template text file
subsection.p: This example shows the required outer structure of a Template text file.

p.extended-example:
Template:
wimp_window {
template_name:"Main"
visible:0,0,640,480
xscroll:0
yscroll:0
next:wimp_TOP
window_flags:wimp_WINDOW_MOVEABLE | wimp_WINDOW_NEW_FORMAT
title_fg:wimp_COLOUR_BLACK
title_bg:wimp_COLOUR_LIGHT_GREY
work_fg:wimp_COLOUR_BLACK
work_bg:wimp_COLOUR_VERY_LIGHT_GREY
scroll_outer:wimp_COLOUR_CREAM
scroll_inner:wimp_COLOUR_ORANGE
highlight_bg:wimp_COLOUR_LIGHT_GREY
extra_flags:
extent:0,-480,640,0
title_flags:wimp_ICON_TEXT | wimp_ICON_INDIRECTED
work_flags:wimp_BUTTON_CLICK
sprite_area:&1
xmin:0
ymin:0
text.text:"Main window"
text.size:12
text.validation:""
}
